what: Doubles and the Summary's step 4 name Tier 1 / 2 / 3 instead of Failure / Marginal / Full Success.
Improvised rolls: you don't always need three results; for a yes or no, Tier 1 fails and Tier 2 or 3 succeeds.
Favored and Doomed Rolls: the numbered list now stands under "Step by step:" above the two examples; the 'roll three dice' sentence is gone.
The Rolls paragraph about Trip being both a Body and an Instinct Action is removed (Rules Language and Chapter 7 keep it).
Saves: a Save Action's DC is 11 + the Modifier or Attribute its traits name; any other Save uses the DC its effect writes, or 13 if none.
foundry: A Save whose effect writes no DC uses DC 13 (a fixed default, not 'usually').

what: Save Actions: Tier 1 is the worst for the target, and a line for two Tiers is written Tier 1 or 2 (the [Mod]-on-Tier-1-and-2 sentence is gone).
Damage on a Card keeps only 'it adds a Modifier or weapon damage only when the card writes [Mod] or [W]'; the Weapon/Power Action sentence and the Power Actions paragraph are removed.
Damage Types no longer says Blunt damage is almost always Vigor.
[C] is removed from the Damage Types list, the Subtypes sentence, the Notation row and the Glossary row.
foundry: If Foundry shows or parses a [C] (origin chooses) damage pool, it no longer exists in the book.

what: The 'Vigor and Resolve are not the Body and Mind Attributes' warning is removed from Damage Types and from the Glossary's [V], [R] row.
The two-damage example is now "[V] 3 + 1d6 Sl + [R] 1d8 Ps".
Damage Subtypes: shortened to two letters, with no mention of [V], [R], [C].
Riders say 'On a Tier line' and 'A Save Action's Tier lines'; the Glossary's Rider row says 'on a Tier line'.
The Cleave section and its Glossary row are removed.
foundry: If Foundry implements or lists Cleave, it is no longer a book rule until a card uses it.

what: Several Targets: the 'rolled per die' paragraph is now one sentence: an Empowered roller's or Save-causer's 1d6! goes to one creature it damages.
The card-label table has a Bloodied, Strained row pointing to Effect Timing.
The "As X AP" paragraph and its three bullets are removed.
The Basic Attack example under the sample cards is removed; the Glossary's Basic Attack row reads [V] 1d4! / 1[W] + [Mod] / 1[W] + 1[D] + [Mod].
The slashes paragraph keeps only: target counts in words, other values in numerals, distances with 'sq.'.
The (T2/T3) Notation row and Chapter 2's 'Some cards mark an effect for some Tiers only' paragraph are removed.
foundry: Foundry should not rely on a (T2/T3) / (T3) tier marker in card text.

what: The Notation row for Critical names all three causes, including three matching dice on a Favored roll.
foundry: A Favored roll with three matching dice is a Critical (already in the Critical section).

what: Up to: a maximum you can go below, even to none, except targets: 'up to three creatures' is one, two or three.
foundry: An 'up to N targets' Action needs at least one target.

what: Bracketed traits: a [Melee] Basic Attack (1A) is a Basic Attack at 1 AP with the Melee trait, whatever else it has; a rule about it doesn't apply to a [Ranged] one.
An encounter can't end while a creature is Dying or Shattered until each stabilizes, gets its damage below its Health Pool, or dies; the tip says an ally can easily get them back up.
A creature that becomes Dying or Shattered outside an encounter rolls on its Table, and that is its roll for the encounter that follows.
foundry: That out-of-combat Table roll counts as the encounter's first-time roll (no second roll when the encounter starts).

what: The three-way initiative example says Mark and the Kobold Mage tie at 13 and the PC goes first.
Swapping Initiative: the AP you had left are frozen and pay for nothing, not even a Reaction (your Reaction Point still can); on your new turn you carry on with them and none becomes Guard.
foundry: After a swap, kept AP can't pay Reactions until your new turn, and they give no Guard at that turn's start.

what: The Reaction Point pays for Reactions and for the few cards that say you spend it (Smite, Steady Draw); the Glossary row says the same.
foundry: Smite's and Steady Draw's Reaction Point spend is legal and outside a Reaction.

what: The Guard from unspent AP lasts until you regain AP at the start of your next turn; Chapter 4 says it lasts until you regain AP again; Rounds says nothing else lasts until the start of your next turn.
foundry: Unspent-AP Guard ends when the creature next regains AP (start of its next turn), not at the end of a round.

what: Unspent AP: the bullet about a kept AP spent on a Reaction is removed, and the next bullet reads only 'Your Reaction Point never becomes Guard.'
Paying: the sentence about a feature giving a second Reaction Point is removed.

An Interrupt happens before the moment it names (example: entering a square adjacent to you); a Trigger after the moment it names, which can be mid-Action (after the first farther square while still moving).
foundry: Reactions fire on the named moment, not before/after the whole triggering Action: a movement Trigger fires mid-move.

what: What a Reaction Responds To keeps only its first sentence; the list of moments and the 'ends a Move Action' sentence are gone.
One sentence: 'Triggering' is used for both kinds of Reaction; an Interrupt has a triggering creature and Action too.
The movement tip now stands under the Reactions list, reworded: make the full movement, the reacting creature says where the Reaction happens, move the token back if it is disrupted.

Disrupting Actions: a Reaction disrupts only when its card says so; an Interrupt's disruption means the Action never starts, a Trigger's stops it where it is. Both Stand-then-Advance examples are removed.
foundry: An Interrupt does not cancel the Action unless its card says it disrupts.

what: Moving closer / away is judged square by square: entering a square nearer (farther) than the one it came from; the repeated sentence is cut.
foundry: A creature running past you moves closer at its first nearer square and away at its first farther square.

what: Moving Closer ends: Evade, Forced Movement and Reposition don't trigger Reactions from movement, so they are never moving closer or moving away; the bullet in Moving Away is removed.
foundry: A Reaction keyed to the Forced Movement itself can still trigger; only movement-based (closer/away) Reactions ignore it.

what: An Action is something a creature does in a fight; most cost AP; every Action is a card.
The paragraph saying an Action's traits appear next to it in the rules is removed.
Requirements: some Actions have a Requirement line, the first of the card's labeled lines.
Chapter 7, Strike, adds: a Strike made as a Linked Action counts toward neither the 3 Strikes nor the shared At-will count, unless its Action says otherwise.
Linked Actions: a required one you can't make stops the Action there (what happened stays, cost paid); an optional one is skipped. The separate 'no valid target' sentence is removed.
foundry: A required Linked Action that fails stops the rest of the Action without refunding or undoing; an optional one is skipped and the Action continues.

what: Example: a card lets you make a Basic Attack (1A); using Basic Attack on its own the same turn is your first use, no At-will Bane.
Targets of Effects: the 'Remember...' sentence is removed.
Effect Timing opens 'Every line of a card says when it happens (see Reading an Action). Two cases need more:' and keeps only the Bloodied/Strained bullet and the semicolon paragraph.
Buffs: the three bullets about single, per-Tier and 0-on-Tier-1 values are removed.
Buffs' first paragraph adds: a Buff that harms the Action it modifies is a Debuff.
The Slowed bullet is removed from Stacking; the lead-in still says 'Five things do add up:' because B1-083 adds a damage-reduction bullet (five again).
At-will: each At-will Action has its own count, except At-will [Strike] Actions, which share one.
Frequency: every Action has a Frequency in its card's title bar; an At-will Action with no roll has no Bane to take.
Round: once per turn-cycle; a Round Reaction used late in one round can't be used early in the next before your own turn starts.
Defenses: one of its three Defenses; some Actions roll against a set DC instead.
EoT: one gained on your own turn ends at its end; one gained on another creature's turn lasts until the end of your next turn.
foundry: An EoT effect gained out of turn lasts until the end of the affected creature's next turn.

what: The initiative slot definition opens Rounds and Durations (with the swap case for EoT); it is gone from End of Encounter, with its repeat of Rounds' parenthesis.
Momentum gaining: +1 after each encounter overcome; until non-fight scenes have rules the GM says which count.
'Never spent' is said once, in Escalation's first paragraph; cut from Chapter 1's Notation row, the Escalation N paragraph, the GM's valve tip and Chapter 5.
Size: the horse sentence is removed.
Squeezing: while a creature stands where it doesn't fit and is not mid-movement, its Rolls are Doomed and it is Vulnerable half its level.
foundry: The squeeze penalty applies while stopped in a too-small space (to act or end the turn), not while passing through.

what: Chapter 7, Move: you can't end in another creature's space nor enter an unwilling creature's space; a willing creature's space is Difficult Terrain.
foundry: Enemy spaces block movement entirely (not Difficult Terrain).

what: Creatures in your way: an Unconscious creature and a dead one are Difficult Terrain; a creature that is Down and still fighting holds its space like any other.
foundry: A Desperate, or Dying/Shattered-and-fighting, creature blocks like a standing one; only Unconscious or dead creatures are passable Difficult Terrain.

what: The Tumble sentence drops '(Footwork's Weave)'.
Pulled: the cone is measured from the square the creature starts in; every path square lies less than 45° off the line from that square to the origin.
foundry: Pull path validation uses a fixed cone from the starting square, not one recomputed each step.

what: The Reposition example says 'Your Reach is 2.'
The creatures'-space rule stays in Movement; Difficult Terrain points to it; Evade says an ally's space is the one exception (see Movement).
Hazardous Terrain: the 'notation, not a trait' sentence is gone; the paragraph starts 'The effect declares its pattern(s) after a colon'.
Weapon Range example: a Pike has Range 3; with Reach 2 it attacks at Range 4.
Leaning lasts until the end of your turn and ends early when you leave your square.
The Emanation example is a creature that slams the ground around itself (no Ground Slam).
The Line example ends 'a different shape, the same number of squares'.
Light: the Lantern of Faith sentence is removed.
Senses table, last column: Obscured '1 Field Boon, if you are Clear to it'; Hidden and Unsensed 'Favored, if you are Clear or Obscured to it'.
foundry: A creature Hidden or Unsensed to you is Favored against you only if you perceive it no better (you are Clear or Obscured to it).

what: Hearing: creatures in combat make noise, even when they don't move.
Hiding: after a non-Subtle Action, Hide ends and each creature perceives you with its own senses again.
The Snake example: its Favored is 5 Boons, less its 1 Field Bane: it rolls normally and adds 4.
Instances of Damage: 'Rules that count instances count them this way' is removed.
Lethal and Nonlethal opens: a Nonlethal Action can deal Lethal damage by taking a Bane, and any other Action can deal Nonlethal by taking a Bane.
The pointer paragraph to Roll Effects and Conditions is removed.
Dominant Damage keeps only 'You know which Dominant Damage a creature has if you perceive them (Hidden is enough).'

Rally Points: 'While Down or Unconscious, you can't use Steel Yourself'; the Unconscious bullet 'You can't wake up while Dying...' is removed. The Chapter 3 text was not written: B1-063's text for the same sentence was applied instead.
foundry: Down is any creature whose damage reaches its Health Pool; Steel Yourself is blocked for all of them and for Unconscious ones.

what: Stacking lists Damage reductions from different effects among the things that add up.
Rest: a safe place is one where you are sure you can rest safely, such as a town; the wilderness is not; the GM decides.
The Glossary's Bloodied, Strained row gives their effects (Speed −2 min 1 and Steadiness −1; no Reaction Point regained).
The Strained tip about where a Bloodied line is written is removed.
The Dying Table's Tier 3: 'You stabilize: you are no longer Dying, but you stay Unconscious.' (no roll); Shattered now uses Dying's tables (B1-090).
foundry: Stabilizing on a Tier 3 rolls no Wound.

what: Shattered is one sentence: it works as Dying, with the Shattered Table, a Mind Check at the end of each turn, and 'giving up' for collapsing; its three tables are gone.
Unconscious: damage while both Unconscious and Down makes you roll on the Dying or Shattered Table (becoming one first if needed); an NPC doesn't roll, NPCs Going Down decides again.
foundry: A Desperate (awake) creature taking damage does not roll on a Table by this bullet; an NPC hit while Unconscious and Down re-runs NPCs Going Down (dies on more Lethal damage).
